analysis:
All three CHANGELOG.md units are documentation only, and no source code is shown. The base excerpts (lines 1327-1791) are historical release notes. The head excerpt (lines 1-221) adds Unreleased entries. Security-relevant claims:
- Line 5: provider cache storage controls, covering an external cache directory, a pinned volume UUID, required encryption, and a persistent write-ledger and keys kept on the Mac. This affects T-041 and TB-007 at-rest posture (flagged).
- Lines 31-41: Autopilot daily earnings floor, with consent evidence, a pool cap, and the Nov 7 end date. Relates to T-060 and TB-006, which already describe reward-administration risks. Admin-only baseline repair and backfill are covered by that threat.
- Lines 9 and 64-72: member-only merge clearance and the Bedrock review workflow. This is CI and review tooling, and the threat model does not cover it.
- Lines 115-121: soft-delete mutations default off; migration timeouts; App Attest production validation before DB access. This is consistent with T-059, T-052 and T-057.
- Lines 126-144: account erasure. Related to T-059; the scrub, fences and outbox appear consistent.
Integration should verify the cache-set code against T-041 (external root, TTL sweep, UUID pinning, key and ledger location) and the Autopilot reward authorization against T-060. No code was available to confirm either.

findings.detail: CHANGELOG.md line 5 adds `darkbloom cache set --directory ...`, which moves encrypted SSD prefix-cache files to an operator-chosen external volume, and pins the volume UUID. T-041 assumes a single on-box root (darkbloom/kv3). It also assumes the 30-minute sliding TTL, the opportunistic sweep and the disk budget bound how long DBK3 artifacts exist. If the external disk is unmounted or replaced, the provider 'refuses ... without falling back', so the sweep cannot run. Encrypted files then persist on a removable, portable device well past the TTL. The HMAC-named files also keep leaking file count, sizes and mtimes. The KEK stays on the Mac, which limits content exposure; the KEK wipe remains the crypto purge. The threat model does not cover this new at-rest location, the TTL-expiry gap for detached media, or the trust placed in the volume UUID and 'encryption required' check. Update T-041 and TB-007 to cover external roots. State that TTL and LRU purge need the volume mounted, and that the KEK wipe is the only purge for detached media. Confirm the encryption check cannot be bypassed by a user-controlled mount.
findings.title: External prefix-cache volume option changes the T-041 at-rest threat model (TTL purge, volume trust)
